newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE MATCHES THIS WEEKEND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE MATCHES THIS WEEKEND.

text.p: The following matches are being played in the English premier league this weekend (league positions in parentheses, all kickoff times 1500 GMT Saturday except Leeds v Chelsea 1600 Sunday and Tottenham v Liverpool 2000 Monday)

Savo Milosevic is poised to make his first appearance at Villa Park for two months, following the collapse of his move to Perugia. Villa, knocked out of the League Cup by Wimbledon on Tuesday, are also hoping Sasa Curcic will recover from a stomach bug. Middlesbrough, who beat Newcastle in the League Cup are expected to be unchanged.

Improving Blackburn could move out of the bottom two positions for the first time for three months against out-of-form Southampton, who will be missing the injured Matt Le Tissier and Alan Nielsen. Greek winger George Donis could return for Blackburn after missing three matches with a groin strain.
Darren Huckerby, who joined Coventry for 1.0 million pounds from Newcastle last week, could make his full debut for a Coventry side without a win for nine games.

Sunderland manager Peter Reid returns to the ground he graced as an Everton player in the 1980s looking for an improvement in his team's form after picking up just five points from a possible 21 -- and without an away goal in their last six league games. In-form Everton should make it eight games unbeaten.

United manager Alex Ferguson is likely to make eight changes to the "reserve" side beaten 2-0 by Leicester in the League Cup on Wednesday. Whatever team he plays United have looked out of sorts lately and a Leicester win is not inconceivable.

Both sides were knocked out of the League Cup on Wednesday -- leaving them more time to concentrate on the title. Arsenal are as resilient as ever under new coach Arsene Wenger as they proved by beating Spurs last Sunday. After three draws and a defeat in their last four games, United need a win.

Sheffield Wednesday have drawn four and won one of their last five while West Ham have drawn their last three -- including a 1-1 draw with Stockport in the league cup. A share of the points looks likely.

Wimbledon have gone 16 matches without defeat, Forest have gone 10 without a win and are bottom. Forest play Newcastle, Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester United after this game -- and on present form will be lucky to get a point from any of them.

Leeds' Ghanain striker Tony Yeboah could return to the squad for the first time since a knee operation in March and manager George Graham could also have Rodney Wallace back from injury in time to face one of his old clubs. In-form Chelsea signed Norwegian goalkeeper Frode Groddas on Friday after a period on loan.

Tottenham suffered arguably the most humiliating defeat in their history losing 6-1 to Bolton in the League Cup on Wednesday. Liverpool beat Tottenham's North London arch-rivals Arsenal 4-2 on Wednesday and Arsenal beat Tottenham 3-1 last Sunday so the omens are not looking too hot for Gerry Francis's beleagured men.
